text: Lose a hundred? They needed two oh two.
Here's the deal. Flip a coin. Heads, you lose a hundred dollars.
Tails, you win. How much would tails have to pay before you'd flip?
Tversky and Kahneman asked twenty-five grad students this, at a computer.
On paper, anything over a hundred is a good bet.
Risk twenty-five, they wanted sixty-one. Risk a hundred fifty, two eighty.
A loss weighs about twice a gain. Six hundred later estimates land near two.
So, lose a hundred. What would you need?
